title: Keys, Lock Changes and the Named Access List on a Safe Deposit Box Lease
content:
A rental of Safe Deposit Boxes carries at most one co-lessee and at most two deputies. The co-lessee and the deputies named on a rental are changed only on the lessee's own signed instruction, and adding a co-lessee carries the charge set for that size.

## Keys

Keys are never duplicated.

A lost key requires a lock change, made as a service charge on the rental at the lock change charge set for that size.

Where every key to a box is lost, the box is drilled at the drilling charge set for that size and the lock is changed at the lock change charge set for that size.

## The two key situations distinguished

| What has happened to the keys | What follows |
| --- | --- |
| One key is lost and another is still held | the lock is changed, at the lock change charge |
| Every key is lost | the box is drilled at the drilling charge, and the lock is changed at the lock change charge |

The distinction is between keys the lessee can still open the box with and no key at all: only in the second case does the box have to be opened by force, and only in that case do two charges arise on the rental rather than one.

## The named access list

The names on a rental are the lessee, at most one co-lessee, and at most two deputies. A change to those names rests on the lessee's own signed instruction; an instruction given by the co-lessee or by a deputy is not that instruction, and neither is one given on the lessee's behalf by anyone else.

A lessee who has mislaid a key and asks for a replacement cut from the bank's pattern is in the same position as any other lessee who has lost a key, since keys are not duplicated: the lock is changed.
